note: v1, THE DRONE (first round; Harry, 12 Nov: "get even a drone in place so we can start the playlist and replace it on round 2"). A placeholder so the groove can open to the song: 48 bars, 1:34, 126 bpm, on the home note F. LISTEN FOR: a bowed low F that never moves, its fifth arriving at 0:15, a ride bell on every quarter-note from 0:15 (the pulse: common time, plainly), and two clean-guitar cells ticking over it - five sixteenths long on the left from 0:08, seven on the right from 0:30 - which drift against the bar and against each other and strike together every 35 sixteenths; one open low string of the 8-string at 0:30 and 1:01. Library patches only; nothing here is the new sound family yet (that is being built and measured against the old one now) and none of it is meant to survive round 2 except the home note, the pulse and the two cells. Measured, not heard: -12.0 LUFS, true peak -1.29, left and right within 1 dB in every 8 bars. compscore 85.9 (length 0 by design: the slot is 12-14 minutes).

note: v2, THE WHOLE PIECE, ROUGH (whole-song round; Harry, 12 Nov: "get the song down so i can start listening to it and then we can refine a great deal over time"). The drone is replaced by all thirteen minutes: 409 bars at 126 bpm, 13:03. WHAT IT IS: one steady pulse in 4/4 that never breaks, and three WHEELS under it - riff cells five, seven and eleven sixteenths long - that start together at bar 1 and keep turning for the whole piece, heard or not. All three meet the bar line again only at bar 386 (5 x 7 x 11 bars later, 12:13): the piece is that wait, and what it lands on is plain common time, a cell eight sixteenths long with the snare on 2 and 4, for the first and only time. On the way two wheels at a time meet on a bar line, and those meetings are the section boundaries (so the form, 35 20 15 7 28 5 30 14 11 10 / 35 / 10 11 14 30 5 28 7 15 20 35 bars, is a palindrome nobody chose); the two that have just met are what the next section is made of. LISTEN FOR: 0:00 one strike of everything, then only clean ticks (five on the left, seven on the right from 0:23, eleven in the middle from 0:42); 1:06 riff A, the five wheel, full band; 1:44 eleven's open chords ringing over it; 2:13 seven bars of the seven wheel nearly alone; 2:26 riff B (seven) with the bass on eleven, and the lead's tune from 2:53 (one note to each turn of the eleven wheel); 3:20 stop-time, sixteen stabs; 3:29 riff C, the eleven wheel, the same shape pulled apart, slow and wide; 4:26 five in the left guitar against seven in the right; 4:53 the lead runs; 5:33 the eye: the ticks alone again, the tune an octave down; 6:40 the weight returns and the sections come back in mirror order, heavier (8:53 the hardest stretch: sixteenth-note kick, a semitone up and back at 9:20); 11:06 the approach, all three wheels at once; 12:13 THE LANDING; 12:43 the last chord rings out over the ticks. A crash marks every bar line where a sounding wheel starts a turn. THE SOUND: the rhythm guitars are the first of the new family, ct-chug-l / ct-chug-r (patches/, sounds.md): the old m8-obzen pair with the engine's white-box amp (triode preamp stages, a push-pull power amp inside a feedback loop driving a speaker), a longer pitch settle on the slack low string, more scrape and sympathetic ring. Measured against two records' guitar stems (tools/riffpunch.py, old pair -> new): Bleed 41.4 -> 67.0, The Faultless 37.8 -> 69.1 (the separators' floor is 67-86); 30 candidates, in ~/.local/state/chirper-zero/c10. A/B on riff A, old rig then new, same notes: http://pocket4:8790/clips/chirper-zero-commontime-rig-old-new-ab.mp3 (full band) and http://pocket4:8790/clips/chirper-zero-commontime-rig-old-new-guitars-only-ab.mp3. Bass, kit, clean guitar and lead are still the old family (bass-fat, obzen-kit-dry, m8-clean, m8-lead-guitar): next. WHAT I MEASURED (I cannot listen): every section's level and left/right (heavy sections -13.3 to -14.6 dBFS rms, the opening -20.9, the eye -20.1; left and right within 0.5 dB except the 7-bar seven break, +1.6 left by design: the right guitar enters four bars late); each track against the mix in three windows (tools/presence.py): the first draft had the cymbals LOUDEST everywhere (2 dB under the mix; now 8.6) and the bass 17 dB under (now 9.4); band shares of the heavy sections against seven records of the genre: inside their range in every band (90-355 Hz 2 dB under their median). -10.0 LUFS, true peak -1.29, no flat-topping. KNOWN ROUGH: the lead in the eye is 9 dB over the ticks (too far forward); the kick is the loudest thing in riff A; the sections differ in which wheels play but not yet enough in style; every fill is the same run; no vocals; nothing has been heard by anyone. compscore 94.46 (the v1 drone 85.9): structure, variety, rhythm, master, length 100; recurrence 68.8 (17 of 21 sections return: too alike). motifs.md, styles.md, sounds.md.

WHAT WAS MEASURED (I cannot listen). SNARE: the engine's physical drum (a stick on two coupled heads, a shell, wires), tightened; tools/drumpunch.py against Bleed's and The Faultless's drum stems, obzen-kit -> this snare with the old cymbals: 44.1 -> 58.7 and 47.1 -> 56.8 (the snare alone 26 -> 67 and 23 -> 40). NOT HEARD BY ANYONE, and exposed: the eye's chords under the tune; the second guitar's fifths over the hook's tritone; the two bars of ticks alone before the landing. THE SCORE FELL, and I kept it: seeds 0 / 11, v3 97.67 / 99.94 -> v4 94.47 / 95.29. All of it is one term, recurrence (86.8 / 100 -> 67.3 / 72.2): the share of sections that closely match an earlier one went from 0.72 / 0.70, exactly on the term's ceiling of 0.70, to 0.76 / 0.75. Every other term is 100. What moved it, from trials on the way: moving sections to other grounds LOWERED the share (0.70, 99.96 on seed 0), and making the hats and the ride audible RAISED it again (0.75): a section whose cymbals nobody could hear counted as different from the others. I would not make a part inaudible for that. LISTEN FOR: (1) THE WALL RIG, new patches ct-wall-l / ct-wall-r: for chords and slow riffs that are left to ring, where ct-chug is for tight muted riffs. A stiffer string that beats, a looser power amp (8 dB of feedback against 18-20, so it follows the speaker), more sag, thicker cabinets with more room, a slow gate. The two rigs alone on the same chords, tight then wall: http://pocket4:8790/clips/chirper-zero-commontime-rig-chug-wall-ab.mp3 . It plays eleven's open chords wherever they sound (1:44, 7:20, 10:28, the approach), the chord over the bass's break (9:46), every big hit, and RIFF C ITSELF (3:29) and its filled return (6:59): the eleven wheel now has its own sound. v4 then v5: riff C http://pocket4:8790/clips/chirper-zero-commontime-v4-v5-riffC-ab.mp3 ; the chords over riff A's five at 1:44 http://pocket4:8790/clips/chirper-zero-commontime-v4-v5-chords-over-five-ab.mp3 ; the bass's break http://pocket4:8790/clips/chirper-zero-commontime-v4-v5-bass-break-ab.mp3 (2) RIFF C GROWS: its first eleven bars are the riff alone on the wall rig (with bass and drums); the open chords join on the tight rig when the ground moves to Bb at 3:50. (3) THE CLEAN GUITAR, new patch ct-clean, on the three ticks (the opening, the eye, the approach, the ring-out): the old one was a bright pluck in a big room; this is a guitar's direct signal - a neck pickup, a string that beats slowly - through a soft compressor and a clean amp, dry, with the song's delay and hall. Alone, old then new: http://pocket4:8790/clips/chirper-zero-commontime-clean-old-new-ab.mp3 ; in the opening http://pocket4:8790/clips/chirper-zero-commontime-v4-v5-opening-ticks-ab.mp3 ; in the eye http://pocket4:8790/clips/chirper-zero-commontime-v4-v5-eye-ab.mp3 (4) the floor-tom pulse at 10:00 is down a little (it read 8 dB under the mix, now 9). WHAT I MEASURED (I cannot listen): BOTH NEW SOUNDS ARE TONE CHOICES, NOT FITTED - there is no bench for ringing chords or for a clean guitar, so nothing says they are closer to a record, only that they differ in the way meant. The wall rig against the tight rig on the same chords, level matched: 2-5 dB more at 90-355 Hz and 1-2 dB less from 355 Hz to 5.6 kHz; in the song the sections it leads moved the same way (riff C +1.1 dB at 90-355 Hz, -1.9 dB at 1.4-5.6 kHz against v4). The clean guitar against the old one, level matched: 3 dB less at 180-355 Hz, 3.5 dB more at 1.4-2.8 kHz, and DARKER at the very top (2 dB less at 5.6-9 kHz, 13 dB less above 9 kHz: a pickup passes little up there; a version through a cabinet lost 18 dB and was dropped). Against the mix where they play: the wall rig 6 dB under in riff C (the kick is the loudest thing), 9 under as chords over riff A's five; the three ticks 8-9 dB under in the opening and 11 under in the eye, where the lead is on top. Riff C by stretch: -14.6 dBFS alone, -12.9 on Bb, -13.2 home. -10.0 LUFS, true peak -1.39, no flat-topping. compscore seeds 0 / 11: v4 94.47 / 95.29 -> v5 95.67 / 98.71; all of the movement is recurrence (67 / 72 -> 75 / 93), the share of sections that closely match an earlier one 0.76 / 0.75 -> 0.74 / 0.71 against a ceiling of 0.70. That term sits on a cliff here and one trial of this same round read 92.5 / 97.3, so take the direction, not the size. note: v7, THE MIX AGAINST ELEVEN RECORDS (palette round; no note changed). I measured where the whole mix's energy sits, in nine bands, in three heavy stretches (riff A, all three wheels, the hardest stretch), beside the same measure on eleven Meshuggah records at 0:30-2:30. The records agree with each other within about 1 dB in every band, so it is a firm target. v6 against their median: 3.9 dB TOO MUCH at 250-500 Hz and 1.9 too much at 500 Hz-1 kHz (the boxy range every modern metal record cuts), 2.2 dB TOO LITTLE at 60-120 Hz (our bass's weight sat on its 44 Hz fundamental; the records leave that octave to the kick and put the bass's weight an octave up), 1.7 too little at 4-8 kHz. WHAT CHANGED: the rhythm guitars lose 5 dB at 350 Hz and 2.5 at 750 Hz; the bass loses 7 dB at 44 Hz and 8 at 350 Hz, gains 7.5 dB at 90 Hz and 4 at 1.5 kHz, and is then compressed hard so that its level is the same on every ground (the 90 Hz boost alone made it 6 dB louder on Db and Eb than on F); the drums lose 6 dB at 400 Hz and gain 4 dB at 5.5 kHz; the tune is 2.5 dB lower where it plays over the riffs (it was the loudest part there; its run at 4:53 and the eye are as they were). RESULT: every band within about 1 dB of the records' median (from below 60 Hz to 8-16 kHz: +0.7 -0.6 +0.7 -0.2 -0.6 +0.1 +0.3 +0.5 +1.1 dB). LISTEN FOR, v6 then v7, same loudness: less box and more air around the kit, the bass heard as a note under the guitars and not only felt, cymbals forward. Riff A http://pocket4:8790/clips/chirper-zero-commontime-v6-v7-mix-riffA-ab.mp3 ; all three wheels with the tune (7:46) http://pocket4:8790/clips/chirper-zero-commontime-v6-v7-mix-all-three-ab.mp3 ; the hardest stretch (8:53) http://pocket4:8790/clips/chirper-zero-commontime-v6-v7-mix-hardest-ab.mp3 ; riff C on the wall rig (3:29) http://pocket4:8790/clips/chirper-zero-commontime-v6-v7-mix-riffC-ab.mp3 ; the lead's run over Db (4:53) http://pocket4:8790/clips/chirper-zero-commontime-v6-v7-mix-solo-ab.mp3 ; the landing http://pocket4:8790/clips/chirper-zero-commontime-v6-v7-mix-landing-ab.mp3 WHAT ELSE I MEASURED (I cannot listen): against the mix where they play (tools/presence.py), the bass is 8 dB under in riff A (it was 10), the cymbals 10 under (were 12.5), the tune 8 under at 7:46 (was 6.4, the loudest part; now the kick and the guitars are); in the lead's run the lead is on top (5 under) and the bass 8 under. Every section is 1.5-2.4 dB down at 355 Hz-1.4 kHz and 2-3 dB up above 5.6 kHz against v6. -10.0 LUFS, true peak -1.46, no flat-topping. The groove plays the unmastered mix: it is level with v6's there (-16.7 LUFS in the full sections, with 1 dB of master gain to make up what the cuts took). The score is at its ceiling (100.00 on both seeds) and says nothing; this is kept on the measurement above. CAVEATS: the per-instrument numbers lean on a stem separator; the whole-mix numbers do not. The bass's compressor is strong (8:1); if the bass now sounds flat or pumps, that is where to look. One band I left alone: the lowest note of the drone in the quiet sections (44 Hz) reads 5 dB over the genre's envelope across the whole song; in the heavy stretches the bottom octave is 0.7 over. note: v8, SLOW CHORDS BEFORE THE EYE (section round: the ten bars at 5:14-5:33). Every heavy section so far was a muted riff; the piece had nothing slow and heavy. v45, THE RUN, BACKWARDS (section round: 6:59-7:20, in the window 7:06-7:37 flagged "static"). The piece is a palindrome: every section before the eye has a mirror after it. The lead guitar's run at 4:53 (eleven bars, on D flat) is the one melody of the first half, and its mirror, the eleven bars at 6:59 on B flat, had no lead at all. Now the run comes back there BACKWARDS, note for note: the same 99 notes with the same lengths, set in a mirror, a minor third lower, the wah pedal's moves mirrored with them. Forwards, each flurry climbs to a long held note. Backwards, each long note comes first and the flurry falls away from it into the next. Its last note is a semitone under the ground the next section lands on. It is the one place where the palindrome is heard in a tune. It sits 3 dB under the run: a thing remembered, not a second solo.
